title: Script stream block reader
summary: Recovered 0x4f60a0 buffered block reader as a member method: returns bytes not read, invokes cdecl refill callback with two opaque contexts and a persistent size slot, copies chunks and advances cursor/count. Original ECX/EDX plus caller-clean stack ABI is represented by a test-only GCC regparm adapter. Zero-extended byte probes cannot signal EOF even for 0xff.
test_description: 1125 differential cases across 0..8 buffered bytes, 0..24 requested bytes, null refill, zero-sized refill, multi-refill, unchanged size slot and partial-read failures. Compare return, destination and canaries, cursor, available count, callback call counts and incoming size history, context/callback fields and surrounding object guards. Includes 0xff, zero and high-bit bytes. Original memcpy import bound to test byte copy.
known_limits: Opaque context meanings and callback implementation are unresolved; controlled callbacks validate only the reader contract.
Invalid pointers, overlapping memcpy ranges, callback exceptions, destructive reentrancy and oversized inaccessible buffers are outside defined tests.
Portable member ABI differs from the original internal caller-clean ECX/EDX convention; no binary compatibility or byte matching claim.
Original byte probes and temporary refill cursor/count stores are retained; fault handling and asynchronous observation are not validated.
